blogPosts.title: How Much Does a Hot Water System Replacement Cost in Melbourne in 2026?
blogPosts.excerpt: Thinking of replacing your hot water system in Melbourne? We break down costs for electric, gas, solar and heat pump – plus installation fees and rebates.
body: If your hot water system has started making strange noises or the water barely gets warm, you're probably due for a replacement. In Melbourne, where winters can drop below 10°C, a reliable hot water system isn't a luxury – it's a necessity. But how much does a replacement actually cost in 2026? The answer depends on the type of system, your home's layout and whether you need same-day installation.

The most common hot water systems in Melbourne are electric storage and gas continuous flow. An electric storage unit (250L) typically costs between $800 and $1,200 for the unit alone, with installation adding $300–$500. Gas continuous flow systems are more popular for their energy efficiency and endless hot water. Expect to pay $1,200–$2,500 for the unit and $400–$700 for installation by a licensed gasfitter.

Solar hot water systems are becoming more common in Melbourne, especially with government rebates. A complete solar setup (including tank and panels) can cost $3,500–$6,000 installed. The Small-scale Technology Certificates (STCs) can knock off $600–$1,000, making it more affordable long-term. Heat pump systems are another energy-efficient option, costing $2,500–$4,500 installed, and they work well in Melbourne’s climate because they extract heat from the air even on cold days.

Location matters for installation costs. If you live in Southbank or inner Melbourne, access is usually easy, so labour costs are lower. But if you're in a heritage-listed house in Fitzroy or a multi-storey townhouse in St Kilda, extra time and equipment may be needed. Mr Emergency always gives a fixed quote before any work – no hidden fees for tricky access.

Don't forget removal and disposal of your old unit. Most plumbers include this in the installation fee, but it's worth asking. Also, check if your home needs a tempering valve – it’s required by Victorian law for all new hot water installations to prevent scalding. That adds around $150–$250 to the total.

The best time to replace your hot water system in Melbourne is before it fails completely. Winter is peak season for emergency callouts. By planning ahead, you can choose the system that suits your home and budget without the stress of a sudden breakdown. Mr Emergency offers same-day installations across Melbourne – call us for a free quote.

One more tip: if your current system is over 10 years old and you're already noticing small leaks or rust, don't wait. A proactive replacement saves you from a cold shower and potential water damage. We’ve seen too many Melbourne homes flooded from a burst storage tank – it’s not worth the risk.

In summary, a hot water system replacement in Melbourne in 2026 can range from $1,100 for a basic electric system to $6,000+ for a solar setup. The key is to get multiple quotes, check for rebates, and choose a licensed plumber who offers a warranty. Mr Emergency backs all installations with a 5-year labour guarantee – peace of mind included.

blogPosts.title: Emergency Plumber in Melbourne: What to Do When a Pipe Bursts
blogPosts.excerpt: A burst pipe can flood your home in minutes. Learn the immediate steps to take and how Mr Emergency Plumbing Melbourne can fix it fast – 24/7.
body: A burst pipe is one of the most stressful emergencies a Melbourne homeowner can face. Water can gush out at 20 litres per minute, causing thousands of dollars in damage within hours. Whether it's a frozen copper pipe in a Mornington Peninsula holiday home or a corroded joint in a Southbank apartment, knowing what to do can save your property.

First, turn off the water at the main stopcock. In most Melbourne homes, this is located near the front of the property or under the kitchen sink. If you can't find it, call a plumber immediately – they can talk you through it. Next, switch off the electricity if water is near any power points or appliances. Safety first.

Open all taps to drain the system and reduce pressure. This helps slow the leak until a plumber arrives. Then, mop up standing water to prevent damage to floors and walls. Use towels, a wet/dry vacuum if you have one, or even a mop. The faster you remove water, the less chance of mould and structural issues.

Now, call an emergency plumber. In Melbourne, Mr Emergency offers a 30-minute response time – even at 2am. Our plumbers carry everything needed to repair burst pipes, from pipe clamps and soldering kits to replacement sections. Most burst pipes can be fixed on the spot without major wall removal.

Why do pipes burst so often in Melbourne? Temperature swings are a big factor. A sudden cold snap can freeze water in exposed pipes, causing them to expand and crack. That's why many burst pipe calls happen after a frosty night. Older homes with uninsulated pipes in roof cavities are particularly vulnerable.

Prevention is better than a crisis. Insulate exposed pipes in your roof and underfloor before winter. Keep your heating on low when you're away to maintain a consistent temperature. If you're renovating, ask your plumber to use flexible PEX piping, which is less prone to bursting than copper.

If you've had a burst pipe, don't just patch it – consider a replacement if the pipe is old or has been repaired before. Repeated bursts in the same spot are a sign of wider corrosion. Mr Emergency can re-route or re-pipe sections of your home to give you long-term peace of mind.

Remember, time is everything. The longer you wait, the more water damage occurs. Call 1300 164 064 anytime – we’ll have a plumber on the way within 30 minutes. We handle the insurance paperwork too, so you can focus on getting back to normal.

blogPosts.title: Blocked Drains in Melbourne: Causes, Prevention & How We Fix Them Fast
blogPosts.excerpt: Blocked drains are a common headache for Melbourne homeowners. Discover the typical causes, how to prevent them, and when to call a pro like Mr Emergency.
body: A blocked drain is more than an inconvenience – it can cause foul odours, slow drainage and even flooding in your yard or bathroom. Melbourne’s combination of clay soil, old infrastructure and heavy rainfall makes blocked drains a frequent issue. Whether you’re in Werribee, Sunbury or the inner city, the causes are often similar.

Tree roots are the number one culprit in Melbourne. Our suburbs are lined with trees, and their roots seek out water in your pipes. Even small cracks can let roots in, and over time they grow into a dense mass that blocks flow completely. Older homes with clay or earthenware pipes are most at risk. That’s why we use CCTV camera inspections to see exactly what’s going on underground.

Grease buildup is another major cause, especially in kitchens. When you pour hot oil down the sink, it cools and solidifies in the pipes, trapping food scraps and creating a sticky blockage. Over time, this can block your entire kitchen line. Simple prevention: scrape grease into the bin, not the sink, and run hot water with detergent weekly.

In outdoor drains, leaves, mud and debris can accumulate after storms. Melbourne’s sudden downpours can overwhelm stormwater drains, especially if they’re already partially blocked. Regularly cleaning your gutters and drain grates helps. If water pools in your yard after rain, you may have a blocked stormwater drain – we can clear it with high-pressure hydro-jetting.

What should you do if you suspect a blocked drain? Don’t use chemical drain cleaners – they often only mask the problem and can damage old pipes. Instead, try a plunger or a drain snake for minor clogs. But if multiple fixtures are backing up, or if you hear gurgling noises, it’s time to call a professional.

Mr Emergency uses state-of-the-art equipment to clear blocks fast. Our hydro-jetting truck blasts water at high pressure to cut through grease, roots and sludge. For persistent tree root problems, we offer pipe relining – a no-dig solution that seals cracks from the inside and prevents roots from re-entering.

Blocked drains can also be a sign of a collapsed pipe. If your sewer line is old and made of terracotta or cast iron, it may have deteriorated. Our CCTV cameras can pinpoint the exact location and condition, so we know whether a simple clean or a full replacement is needed. We always explain your options before starting work.

If you’re dealing with a slow drain or a full blockage in Melbourne, don’t wait – it usually gets worse. Call Mr Emergency for a fast, no-obligation quote. We cover all suburbs from the Mornington Peninsula to the northern growth corridors. 30-minute response, 24/7 – that’s our promise.

blogPosts.title: Gas Heater Installation in Melbourne: Everything You Need to Know
blogPosts.excerpt: Thinking of installing a gas heater in Melbourne? We cover types, costs, safety requirements and why choosing a licensed gasfitter is essential.
body: Melbourne winters can be brutal, and a reliable gas heater is a popular choice for keeping homes warm without sky-high electricity bills. Gas heating is efficient, heats up fast and works even during power outages. But installing a gas heater isn't a DIY job – it requires a licensed gasfitter who understands Victorian regulations and your home's specific needs.

There are several types of gas heaters available in Melbourne. The most common are wall furnaces (also called space heaters) that mount on an internal wall and draw air from outside. They’re affordable and effective for single rooms. For whole-house heating, ducted gas heating is the go-to – it distributes warm air through vents in each room. Gas log fires and flued gas heaters add ambiance and warmth to living areas.

Costs vary widely. A basic wall furnace installation can start from $1,200 including the unit and labour. Ducted gas heating for a three-bedroom home typically ranges from $4,000 to $7,000. Gas log fires start at around $2,500 installed. These prices include the heater, flue, gas line connection and compliance testing. Always get a fixed quote upfront – Mr Emergency provides transparent pricing with no hidden extras.

Safety is paramount. Victorian law requires that all gas heating installations comply with AS/NZS 5601 and local regulations. A qualified gasfitter will check the flue location, ensure adequate ventilation and test for carbon monoxide. Carbon monoxide is a silent killer – you can't see it or smell it. That's why we always install a carbon monoxide detector as part of the service.

Where in Melbourne you live can affect installation costs. If you’re in a heritage home in Fitzroy or a townhouse in South Yarra, running new gas lines may be more complex. Ground-floor apartments are easier than upper levels. Mr Emergency assesses access during the free site visit and gives you the full picture before any work begins.

When should you install a gas heater? Autumn is the best time – you avoid the winter rush and have your system ready before the cold hits. Many Melbourne homeowners leave it too late and end up on a waitlist. Plan ahead and book your installation in March or April for a stress-free winter.

If you already have ducted gas heating, regular servicing keeps it running efficiently. We recommend a service every two years. A technician will clean the burner, check the heat exchanger and test the flue. Neglected heaters can develop cracks that leak carbon monoxide – a cheap service is better than a tragedy.

For a free quote on gas heater installation in Melbourne, call Mr Emergency. We’re licensed, insured and cover all suburbs. From a small wall furnace in a Brunswick flat to a full ducted system in a Toorak mansion, we’ve installed it all. 30-minute response on emergencies – but for installations, we’ll schedule a time that suits you.
